analysis.title: Americas Technology: Internet - Q3'26 EPS Review: Where to from Here? Recapping Takeaways & Debates - Investor Focus Squarely on Forward Capital Allocation
key_insights: Q3'26 internet earnings reactions showed outsized volatility, driven by perceived AI revenue outcomes against expectations, the sources and uses of capital for AI capex, a reversal of the agentic commerce disruption fear, a stable consumer backdrop, and the evolving marketing funnel around Google Search and AI Mode.

Aggregate capex across AMZN, GOOGL, META and SPCX exceeded $170bn in Q3 alone. The hyperscalers increasingly rely on outside capital, both debt and equity, to fund power generation and data center capacity.
Consumer internet and media platforms that stressed capital discipline, cut content and operating expenses, and expanded high-margin retail media were rewarded this season.

GS says the hyperscalers need to better explain where they have a right to win, which platform and product initiatives are needed at scale, how deep and long the investment cycle is, and what financial framework supports a return over 2-5 years. It views these questions as largely unanswered.

Among large caps, GS highlights Amazon (AMZN), SpaceX (SPCX) and Uber (UBER) as particularly compelling risk/reward from current levels, based on its estimates and upside/downside valuation scenarios.

Cloud: AWS revenue growth accelerated to +39% YoY with backlog of ~$578bn. Google Cloud grew +103% YoY with backlog of ~$561bn and operating margin of ~36%. Combined backlog is above ~$1.1tn. Demand continues to exceed available compute capacity.

AMZN guided to AWS revenue growth of +40% in 2027 and 2028 and expects to offer Trainium outside AWS in late 2027. TPU system sales are becoming a more meaningful part of Google Cloud revenue. Custom silicon is emerging as a competitive and economic differentiator.

The cloud debate has shifted from demand to capacity deployment, monetization, durability of contracted demand, funding, free cash flow and ROIC, with infrastructure spending elevated into 2027 and beyond.

Digital advertising is constructive, led by measurable lower-funnel and performance advertising at scaled platforms using AI targeting (Performance Max, Advantage+, Performance+). Dispersion is rising: RDDT flagged traffic headwinds from Google Search changes, and PINS showed UCAN reacceleration with some pressure in Europe.
GOOGL and META face questions on the timing and size of AI returns, rising depreciation and whether AI monetization justifies the capital intensity.

eCommerce results were broadly constructive. AMZN retail mix is shifting to lower-ASP essentials and grocery. W gained share, ETSY showed improving buyer trends, GRPN remained mixed. The key long-term debate is who owns the consumer relationship in agentic commerce.

Online travel demand is resilient and broadly stable, with pockets of international softness. Platforms are expanding (BKNG Connected Trip, EXPE B2B, ABNB hotels and services) and reiterating capital returns. Debates cover normalized growth, share, AI/agentic discovery, non-marketing investment and buybacks.

Mobility demand is healthy and accelerating in the US. Uber expects autonomous supply to grow from ~700 fully driverless vehicles at YE26 to 2,000+ by YE27. Lyft began integrating Waymo in September. Uber One has 55mm+ members.

Streaming: Spotify shows strong premium subscriber growth and progress toward double-digit ad growth. Netflix faces softer US engagement and near-term ad execution headwinds. WBTN is mixed but improving, with weakness in Japan. STUB shows healthy live events demand.

Gaming: GTA VI is a catalyst expected to reactivate lapsed gamers, and Roblox is targeting the over-18 user market. Mobile gaming is mixed, with Color Block Jam showing double-digit declines offset by Toon Blast and Words with Friends.

Online dating: Tinder DAUs returned to YoY growth for the first time in ~3.5 years. Hinge is expanding into India and Japan. Grindr engagement rose to ~70 minutes per day from ~60, and the company is investing in health and wellness after acquiring Freddie.

Online gambling: core sports betting is healthy, and prediction markets are becoming a real growth vector. DKNG is raising promotion and marketing spend, and SRAD is seeing revenue contribution. Near-term pressure comes from sports rights and prediction-market investment.
Online education: DUOL DAU growth accelerated to +29% YoY and bookings growth to +12% YoY, up ~400bps QoQ. COUR is integrating Udemy and positioning AI as raising demand for upskilling.

Online marketplaces: search traffic pressure is a headwind for UPWK and FVRR, which are launching MCP/LLM integrations. Enterprise and higher-value activity is growing at double-digit rates and offsetting weaker transactional cohorts. Forward margin trajectories diverge.

Sensor Tower data through October 2026 shows Threads (+34% US WAU YoY) and Pinterest (+12%) leading ad platforms, and Netflix WAU down 12% in the US. Online travel apps show broad YoY declines in WAU and sessions. Kalshi MAU in the US is up 136% YoY.
Post-report stock moves (T-1 to T+1) were weak for the large hyperscalers: GOOGL -11%, META -7%, AMZN -6%, and SPCX +8%. RDDT fell -32% and TRIP -31%, while ZIP rose 75% and APP rose 45%.

sector_views.rationale: AI infrastructure demand is strong and cloud is accelerating, but the debate has moved to deployment pace, funding, free cash flow and ROIC.
GS calls the environment constructive, especially for performance advertising, though results are increasingly platform-specific.
Results were broadly constructive, with improving customer health and operating leverage. The long-term question is who owns the consumer in agentic commerce.
Demand is resilient, but there are pockets of international softness and open debates on growth normalization and AI discovery.
US mobility demand is healthy and accelerating, and subscriptions and AVs are scaling.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported: AWS revenue growth +39% YoY and Google Cloud +103% YoY, with Google Cloud operating margin ~36%. Combined cloud backlog is ~$1.1tn+ (AMZN ~$578bn, GOOGL ~$561bn).

Hyperscaler Q3'26 vs consensus (FactSet, as reported): META revenue +2% and profit -21%, AMZN revenue 0% and profit +7%, SPCX revenue +13% and profit +37%, GOOGL revenue 0% and profit -6%. Google and Amazon profit is GAAP EBIT, and all others are adj. EBITDA.
Q3'26 forward-quarter guidance vs consensus: META revenue +1%, AMZN revenue 0% and profit -7%.

Q3'26 online travel vs consensus: BKNG revenue +37% and profit +109%, ABNB revenue +3% and profit +6%, EXPE revenue +4% and profit +9%, TRIP revenue -2% and profit -17%. Post-report moves: BKNG +14%, ABNB +8%, EXPE -5%, TRIP -31%.

Q3'26 ad platforms vs consensus: APP revenue +5% and profit +7% (stock +45% post-report), RDDT revenue +2% and profit +2% with guidance -3% (stock -32%), PINS revenue -3% and profit -3% with guidance -4% and -7% (stock -7%), SNAP revenue 0% and profit +14% (stock -9%).

Q3'26 streaming and gaming vs consensus: NFLX revenue 0% and profit +5% (stock -7%), SPOT revenue 0% and profit 0% (stock +11%), WBTN profit -47% (stock +3%), RBLX bookings +4% and profit +43% (stock -19%), TTWO revenue +3% (stock +5%).
Q3'26 mobility vs consensus: UBER revenue/bookings +1%, profit +1% (stock +3%). LYFT revenue -5%, profit +6% (stock -9%).
Q3'26 online education: DUOL revenue +2%, bookings +3%, profit +4% vs consensus (stock +19%). COUR revenue +2%, profit +12% vs consensus, forward guidance -3% (stock -26%).
Q3'26 online dating: MTCH Adj. EBITDA +4% above consensus and GRND +6%. Tinder DAUs grew YoY for the first time in ~3.5 years.
Q3'26 online gambling: DKNG revenue -5% vs consensus and a 397% profit variance (stock -20%). SRAD revenue +1%, profit +10% (stock +13%). GENI revenue +3%, profit +2% (stock -15%).
risk_factors: Funding risk: hyperscalers rely on outside debt and equity capital for AI infrastructure and power, which pressures free cash flow.
Capacity deployment and durability of contracted cloud demand as supply comes online.
Rising depreciation expense from AI capex weighs on future earnings power, and AI returns may not justify capital intensity.
Traffic dependence on Google Search at RDDT, UPWK and FVRR as AI Mode and zero-click results change discovery.
Agentic commerce could shift who owns the consumer relationship, affecting customer acquisition cost, advertising and marketplace economics.
Netflix faces softer US engagement and near-term ad execution headwinds.
Online gambling faces regulatory uncertainty, sports rights costs and prediction-market investment.
Sensor Tower data shows broad YoY declines in WAU and sessions across online travel apps and some e-commerce apps.

tension_points.bull_case: AI infrastructure demand is exceptionally strong, with AWS at +39% and Google Cloud at +103% YoY, a combined backlog above ~$1.1tn, and demand exceeding available compute capacity.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated capex pressures free cash flow and increases reliance on outside debt and equity. Questions remain on depth and duration of the investment cycle, rising depreciation and whether returns justify spend.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Companies that cannot articulate a strategic and financial framework supporting a positive return on AI investments over the next 2-5 years would weaken the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: AI Mode and Gemini integration raise the value of high-intent ad inventory, and Google Cloud growth is strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Traffic is shifting to synthesized, zero-click environments, creating traffic headwinds for dependents such as RDDT, UPWK and FVRR.
